Title: What Is Diabetes? Causes, Types, and Metabolism Overview
Organization: National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases (NIDDK), NIH
Key Finding: Metabolism is the biological process converting food into energy. Glucose is the primary circulating sugar used by cells for fuel, regulated by pancreatic insulin secretion and liver glycogen storage. Cellular metabolism is an integrated network rather than a single metric.
Notes: Human verified against NIH/NIDDK published clinical overview. Verifies that glucose is cellular fuel and metabolism involves organ crosstalk.

Title: Prediabetes – Your Chance to Prevent Type 2 Diabetes
Organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
Key Finding: Metabolic health risks are cumulative and interconnected. A single elevated reading does not determine lifelong outcome. Structured lifestyle habits including regular physical activity, balanced dietary patterns, and restorative sleep substantially enhance insulin sensitivity without extreme restriction.
Notes: Human verified against CDC National Diabetes Prevention Program data. Confirms lifestyle multi-factor impact without shame.

Title: Healthy Diet Factsheet (Key Principles for Cardiometabolic Health)
Key Finding: Dietary patterns high in diverse vegetables, legumes, whole grains, nuts, and unsaturated fats support metabolic balance. No isolated miracle ingredient can substitute for overall nutrition, physical activity, and adequate rest.
Notes: Human verified against WHO global nutritional factsheet. Confirms holistic whole-food patterns over single "superfood" miracle claims.

Title: Metabolic Syndrome – Definition, Risk Factors, and Clinical Criteria
Key Finding: Metabolic syndrome is defined by a cluster of co-occurring cardiometabolic factors: elevated fasting glucose, high serum triglycerides, low HDL cholesterol, elevated blood pressure, and abdominal waist measurement. Assessing multiple biomarkers together provides a significantly more comprehensive picture than any single measurement in isolation.
Notes: Human verified against MedlinePlus clinical summary. Directly grounds the core campaign thesis that metabolic health is a multi-parameter cluster.

Title: Physical Activity Guidelines for Americans (2nd Edition)
Organization: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS / CDC)
Key Finding: Physical activity induces acute contraction-mediated glucose uptake into skeletal muscle independently of insulin. Regular moderate movement maintains postprandial glucose regulation and vascular elasticity across all body types.
Notes: Human verified against HHS federal guidelines. Affirms movement benefits for insulin sensitivity without promoting weight-shaming or extreme workouts.

Title: Standards of Care in Diabetes — Comprehensive Medical Evaluation
Key Finding: Biomarkers including continuous glucose metrics, fasting glucose, and HbA1c require individual clinical context. Personal health assessments should be conducted with a qualified healthcare professional who considers individual medical history.
Notes: Human verified against ADA clinical guidelines. Supports disclaimer requirement and clinical context nuance.
